taskVersion.name: pilot-ves-label-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Opiro, Etche LGA survey stations. Interpreted layer model from the published survey:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 54.639 | 0.2147 | 0.2147
2 | 9147.8 | 0.30305 | 0.51774
3 | 1119.9 | 21.107 | 21.625
4 | 2566.8 | - | -

The paper labels this station's curve as A-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Opiro, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the paper's curve-type label does not fit the layer values.

**Site Note — Station Opiro, Etche LGA**

Four geoelectric layers were resolved. Layer 1 is a thin, low-resistivity topsoil (54.6 ohm-m, 0.21 m). Layer 2 is an extremely resistive thin horizon (9147.8 ohm-m, 0.30 m), most likely dry, compacted or lateritic/indurated material. Layer 3 (1119.9 ohm-m) is the thickest unit at 21.1 m, extending to 21.6 m depth, and Layer 4 (2566.8 ohm-m) is the infinite basal layer.

Applying the three-layer rule in depth order: layers 1-2-3 give 54.6 < 9147.8 > 1119.9 = **K**; layers 2-3-4 give 9147.8 > 1119.9 < 2566.8 = **H**. The curve is therefore **KH**.

This does not agree with the published A-type label, which would require resistivity to increase steadily with depth; the data instead show a pronounced resistive spike in layer 2. Treat the published label as an error and use KH. Resistivities are high throughout; drilling should target deeper horizons beyond 21.6 m for water.

{"curve_type_stated": "KH", "label_issue_flagged": true}
